proposed.text: Under BP 344, how many horizontal (level) steps must be provided at both the top and bottom of an accessible escalator to allow safe transition onto and off the moving steps?

options.text: At least 2 horizontal steps at the bottom and 1 at the top entry zone
At least 3 horizontal steps at both the top and bottom entry/exit zones
At least 5 horizontal steps at both the top and bottom entry/exit zones
At least 1 horizontal step at both top and bottom, plus a tactile warning strip

rationale.summary: BP 344 IRR requires at least 3 horizontal steps at both the top and bottom of an escalator.
rationale.explanation: The 3 horizontal steps at each end create a level transition zone where users can gain or release their footing before the steps begin rising or after they flatten. Fewer steps reduce safe boarding time, particularly for users with mobility impairments. This is an escalator-specific requirement distinct from the tactile depth specification.
common_misconceptions: Thinking the horizontal step count differs between top and bottom — it is 3 at both ends
Confusing horizontal steps with tactile warning block depth (600 mm)

proposed.explanation: 3 horizontal steps at top and bottom is the BP 344 IRR escalator requirement for safe PWD transition.
